name: SER baseline causal chain (D' / G' geometric-mean aggregation)
description: Operationalises the paper's headline efficiency definition (Eq. 1-3). The Synergistic Efficiency Ratio (SER) is a multiplicative aggregation of normalized dry-matter reduction (D') and nitrogen recovery (G'), each computed on the same matched mass-balance boundary. This DAG isolates the upstream operator-controllable inputs (substrate mass, nitrogen mass, species/feedstock choice) from the mediator pair (D', G') that the paper explicitly says are computed from measured replicate-level balances, not derived from SER itself.
paper_reference: BOS_Paper1_JCP_FINAL.docx, paper line 36-43 (Eq. 1-3 definitions), line 20 (SER as multiplicative index), line 40 (D'/G' computed from measured balances, not from SER).

nodes.description: Input dry matter [kg]. Operator-controllable substrate mass (Eq. 1 denominator).
Input nitrogen [kg]. Operator-controllable via feedstock choice (Eq. 2 denominator).
Discrete stratum: which insect species (e.g. BSF_LARVA, T_MOLITOR). Affects both d_prime and g_prime through biology.
Discrete stratum: substrate composition (e.g. FOOD_WASTE_MIXED, DISTILLERS_GRAIN). Confounds dm_in and n_in via composition correlation.
Recovered dry matter [kg]. Direct mass-balance variable on the Eq. 1 numerator path; not separately manipulable.
Recovered nitrogen [kg]. Direct mass-balance variable on the Eq. 2 numerator path.
Normalized deconstruction rate D' = 1 - DM_out/DM_in (Eq. 1). Bounded in [0, 1]. Computed from measured replicate-level balances.
Normalized nitrogen recovery G' = N_rec,total / N_in (Eq. 2). Bounded in [0, 1]. Computed from measured replicate-level balances.
System Efficiency Ratio SER = sqrt(D' x G') (Eq. 3). Bounded in [0, 1]. The headline outcome.

edges.paper_quote: D' = 1 - DM_out / DM_in (Eq. 1). D' is computed from measured replicate-level mass and N balances on the same matched boundary; neither is derived from SER.
G' = N_rec,total / N_in. G' is computed from measured replicate-level N balance on the matched boundary.
SER = sqrt(D' x G') (Eq. 3). SER aggregates D' and G' into a single replicate-level endpoint.
(implicit: species biology drives deconstruction efficiency; see paper claim #10 in reconnaissance §3.1 — T. brevitarsis reached substantially higher CEA than PB-only larvae)
(implicit: feedstock composition determines dry-matter ratio at fixed feed mass)
(implicit: feedstock total-N fraction determines N_in at fixed feed mass; paper Eq. 2 nomenclature: 'N_in is feed dry mass multiplied by feed total-N concentration')

intended_question: What is the average causal effect of substrate-mass-and-nitrogen input policy on SER, with d_prime and g_prime as the natural mediators? When d_prime and g_prime each rise by 0.1, what is the implied SER lift along Eq.3? Identifies via back-door adjustment on {species_code, feedstock_code}.
small_sample_warning: Paper experiment has n = 4 replicates per arm (paper line 48 reports 'observed SER SD ~0.03 ... 96% power to detect Delta-Delta-SER = 0.10 at alpha=0.05 with n=4 per group' — power calc is for SER difference, not for a causal ATE estimator). Phase B evidence_level will auto-clamp to 'planned' when n_used_per_stratum < n_min_per_stratum (default 30).
notes_for_user_review: DAG 001 is the most directly paper-anchored of the three. Every edge except the two 'confounding' species/feedstock edges is a literal Eq. 1-3 mechanical relationship. The two confounding edges encode domain knowledge that the paper does not formalise but which is necessary for identification.
